title: AuthBench v2.2.0: temporally leak-free, alert-budget evaluation of authentication anomaly detectors
description:
AuthBench is an open harness that evaluates authentication anomaly detectors under a temporally leak-free protocol and daily alert budgets. It checks the temporal order of its partitions, tests that every detector scores an event identically alone or among others, ranks events, edge-hours and user-days within each day, gives every red-team campaign the daily budget at which it is first detected, and sets each result against its exact distribution under a random ranking and against label-free activity rankings of the same units.

Version 2.2.0 corrects the favourable end of the tie bracket of campaign recall: it is now the exact maximum over tie orders, computed as a matching of campaigns to the places in contention and checked against every tie order on small cases. Two values of report version 2 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23687498) change: the favourable bracket of pair rarity (M2a) at 10 alerts per day moves from 32.1% to 34.0% in the harmonised protocol and from 32.7% to 38.5% in the temporal protocol. The values at 500 alerts per day, the demo tables and the run outputs of 22 October 2026 are unchanged. The methodology note no longer says that get_test_split is the only path to the test partition, and the account-grouped bootstrap test can now fail.

Version 2.1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23623196) is the code of report version 2.
